headings: Underwriting Criteria and Due Diligence Process
paragraphs: Farmland Partners Inc. ("FPI"), collectively with its subsidiaries, is an internally managed real estate company that owns and seeks to acquire high-quality farmland located in agricultural markets throughout North America. FPI was incorporated in Maryland on September 27, 2013. FPI elected to be taxed as a real estate investment trust ("REIT") under Sections 856 through 860 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code"), commencing with its short taxable year ended December 31, 2014.

FPI is the sole member of the sole general partner of Farmland Partners Operating Partnership, LP (the "Operating Partnership"), which was formed in Delaware on September 27, 2013. All of FPI's assets are held by, and its operations are primarily conducted through, the Operating Partnership and the wholly owned subsidiaries of the Operating Partnership. As of December 31, 2025, FPI owned a 98.1% interest in the Operating Partnership. See "Note 9—Stockholders' Equity and Non-controlling Interests" for additional discussion regarding Class A Common units of limited partnership interest in the Operating Partnership ("Common units"), Series A preferred units of limited partnership interest in the Operating Partnership ("Series A preferred units") and Series B participating preferred units of limited partnership interest in the Operating Partnership ("Series B participating preferred units"). Unlike holders of FPI's common stock, par value $0.01 per share ("common stock"), holders of the Operating Partnership's Common units and Series A preferred units generally do not have voting rights or the power to direct the affairs of FPI. As the sole member of the sole general partner with control of the Operating Partnership, FPI is the primary beneficiary and therefore consolidates the Operating Partnership in accordance with accounting standards for consolidation of variable interest entities.
References to the "Company," "we," "us," or "our" mean collectively FPI and its consolidated subsidiaries, including the Operating Partnership.

Our primary strategic objective is to utilize our position as a leading institutional acquirer, owner and manager of high-quality farmland located in agricultural markets throughout North America to deliver strong risk adjusted returns to investors through a combination of cash dividends and asset appreciation. As of December 31, 2025, we owned farms with an aggregate of approximately 71,600 acres in Arkansas, California, Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Louisiana, Missouri, Nebraska, South Carolina, Texas and West Virginia. In addition, as of December 31, 2025, we owned land and buildings for four agriculture equipment dealerships in Ohio leased to Ag Pro Ohio, LLC ("Ag Pro") under the John Deere brand. As of December 31, 2025, the Operating Partnership owned a 9.97% equity interest in Promised Land Opportunity Zone Farms I, LLC (the "OZ Fund"), an unconsolidated equity method investment, that holds 11 properties (see "Note 1—Organization and Significant Accounting Policies—Equity Method Investments"). As of December 31, 2025, approximately 60% of our owned portfolio (by value) was used to grow primary crops, such as corn, soybeans, wheat, rice and cotton, and approximately 40% was used to produce specialty crops, such as almonds, pistachios, citrus, avocados, strawberries, and edible beans. We believe our portfolio gives investors the economic benefit of increasing global food demand in the face of growing scarcity of high-quality farmland and will continue to reflect the approximate allocation of U.S. agricultural output between primary crops and animal protein (whose production relies principally on primary crops as feed), on one hand, and specialty crops, on the other.

In addition, we offer a loan program (the "FPI Loan Program") pursuant to which we make loans to landowners with whom we have established relationships and third-party farmers (both tenant and non-tenant) to provide financing for business operations, property acquisitions, working capital requirements, operational farming activities, farming infrastructure projects and non-farming business needs.

FPI Agribusiness Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary (the "TRS" or "FPI Agribusiness"), is a taxable REIT subsidiary that was formed to provide volume purchasing services to the Company's tenants and to directly operate farms under certain circumstances. As of December 31, 2025, the TRS performed direct farming operations on 1,845 acres of permanent crop farmland owned by the Company located in California.

FPI strategically seeks opportunities to generate incremental revenues with environmentally friendly usage of our farmland. We have long-term lease arrangements on certain farm properties pursuant to which operators engage in solar and wind energy production. As of December 31, 2025, 10 of our farms, which collectively comprised approximately 1,973 acres, had leases for operational or under-construction renewable energy production, and 12 of our farms, which collectively comprise approximately 4,211 acres, had options for potential future solar or wind development and operating lease. Refer to "–Sustainability" for more information.

Our principal source of revenue is rent from tenants that conduct farming operations on our farmland pursuant to leases with terms ranging primarily from one to three years. The majority of the leases that are in place as of the date of this Annual Report on Form 10-K have fixed rent payments. Some of our leases have variable rents based on the revenue generated by our farm-operator tenants. We believe that this mix of fixed and variable rents will help insulate us from the variability of farming operations and reduce our credit-risk exposure to farm-operator tenants while making us an attractive landlord in certain regions where variable leases are customary. However, we may be exposed to tenant credit risk and farming operation risks, particularly with respect to leases that do not require advance payment of 100% of the fixed rent, variable rent arrangements and leases with terms greater than one year.
● Net income decreased 47.6% from $61.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2024 to $32.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2025;

● Adjusted Funds from Operation ("AFFO") increased 27% from $14.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024 to $17.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2025; AFFO per weighted average common share increased 34.5% from $0.29 per share available to common stockholders for the year ended December 31, 2024 to $0.39 per share available to common stockholders for the year ended December 31, 2025;

● We completed dispositions of 60 properties in the Corn Belt, Delta and South, High Plains and West Coast regions for aggregate consideration of $90.2 million, including $2.1 million in seller financing, and recognized an aggregate net gain on sale of $34.9 million. Of the 60 property dispositions, 23 properties were exchanged for the redemption and cancellation of 31,000 Series A preferred units;
● We completed acquisitions of six properties in the Corn Belt region for total consideration of $7.3 million;
● Total indebtedness decreased $43.0 million from $204.6 million at December 31, 2024 to $161.6 million at December 31, 2025;
● We repurchased 3,411,581 shares of our common stock at a weighted average price of $11.07 per share;

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Properties
Mortgage debt obligations expose us to the possibility of foreclosure, which could result in the loss of our investment in a property or group of properties subject to mortgage debt.

Our debt financing agreements may restrict our ability to engage in certain business activities, including our ability to incur additional indebtedness, make capital expenditures and make certain investments.

Increases in benchmark interest rates will increase our borrowing costs, which will negatively impact our financial condition, results of operations, growth prospects and ability to make distributions to stockholders.
Increases in interest rates will increase our tenants' borrowing costs and make it more difficult for them to obtain credit and may cause land prices to decline.
Global economic conditions, including elevated levels of inflation and supply chain disruptions, could materially and adversely affect our and our tenants' operations.
Approximately 60% of our portfolio is comprised of properties used to grow primary crops such as corn, soybeans, wheat, rice and cotton, which subjects us to risks associated with primary row crops.
Investments in farmland used for permanent/specialty crops have a higher risk profile than farmland used for annual row crops.
Failure to succeed in new markets may have adverse consequences.
We do not continuously monitor and evaluate tenant credit quality, and our financial performance may be subject to risks associated with our tenants' financial condition and liquidity position.

We may be unable to collect balances due on our leases from any tenants in financial distress or bankruptcy, which could materially and adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations and cash flow.
Illiquidity of real estate investments could significantly impede our ability to respond to adverse changes in the performance of our properties and harm our financial condition.
Some state laws prohibit or restrict the ownership of agricultural land by business entities, which could impede the growth of our portfolio and our ability to diversify geographically.
We may be subject to unknown or contingent liabilities related to acquired properties and properties that we may acquire in the future, which could have a material adverse effect on us.

The loss of key management personnel, particularly Paul A. Pittman and Luca Fabbri, could have a material adverse effect on our ability to implement our business strategy and to achieve our investment objectives.
Joint venture investments could be adversely affected by our lack of sole decision-making authority, our reliance on co-venturers' financial condition and disputes between us and our co-venturers.
We may fail to realize some or all of the anticipated benefits of our ownership interest in the OZ Fund.
Liability for uninsured or underinsured losses could materially and adversely affect our financial condition and cash flow.

We have previously been subject to, and may in the future be subject to, litigation or threatened litigation, which may require us to pay damages and expenses or restrict the operation of our business.
We may incur significant unrecoverable costs if we are not successful in connection with the litigation we have filed against Sabrepoint.
Potential liability for environmental matters could materially and adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
paragraphs: Set forth below are the risks that we believe are material to our stockholders. You should carefully consider the following risks in evaluating our Company and our business. The occurrence of any of the following factors, events or circumstances described below could materially adversely impact our financial condition, results of operations, cash flow, the market price of shares of our common stock and preferred stock and our ability to, among other things, satisfy our debt service obligations and to make distributions to our stockholders, which in turn could cause our stockholders to lose all or a part of their investment. Some statements in this report including statements in the following risk factors constitute forward-looking statements. Please refer to the section entitled "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" at the beginning of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Our business is dependent in part upon the profitability of our tenants' farming operations, and a sustained downturn in the profitability of their farming operations could have a material adverse effect on the amount of rent we can collect and, consequently, our cash flow and ability to make distributions to our stockholders.

We depend on our tenants to operate the farms we own in a manner that generates revenues sufficient to allow them to meet their obligations to us, including their obligations to pay rent and real estate taxes, maintain certain insurance coverage and maintain the properties generally. The ability of our tenants to fulfill their obligations under our leases depends, in part, upon the overall profitability of their farming operations, which could be adversely impacted by, among

other things, adverse weather conditions, crop prices, crop disease, pests, and unfavorable or uncertain political, economic, business, trade or regulatory conditions. We are susceptible to any decline in the profitability of our tenants' farming operations, to the extent that it would impact their ability to pay rents. In addition, many farms are dependent on a limited number of key individuals whose injury or death may affect the successful operation of the farm. We can provide no assurances that, if a tenant defaults on its obligations to us under a lease, we will be able to lease or re-lease that farm on economically favorable terms in a timely manner, or at all. In addition, we may experience delays in enforcing our rights as landlord and may incur substantial costs in protecting our investment.

As a result, any downturn in the profitability of the farming operations of our tenants or a downturn in the farming industry as a whole could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations, cash flow and ability to make distributions to our stockholders.

We have a substantial amount of indebtedness outstanding, which may expose us to the risk of default under our debt obligations, restrict our operations and our ability to grow our business and revenues and restrict our ability to pay distributions to our stockholders.

As of December 31, 2025, we had access to liquidity of $172.9 million, consisting of $9.3 million in cash and $163.6 million in undrawn availability under our credit facilities with Federal Agricultural Mortgage Corporation and its wholly owned subsidiary, Farmer Mac Mortgage Securities Corporation (collectively, "Farmer Mac"), Metropolitan Life Insurance Company ("MetLife"), and Rutledge Investment Company ("Rutledge") compared to cash of $78.4 million and $167.4 million in undrawn availability under our credit facilities as of December 31, 2024. paragraphs: Farmland Partners Inc. ("FPI"), 合併其子公司後，為一家 internally managed real estate 公司，擁有並尋求取得位於北美各農業市場的高品質農地。FPI 於 2013 年 9 月 27 日在馬裏蘭州成立。FPI 選擇以 real estate investment trust ("REIT") 被課稅，根據 1986 年內政部稅法第 856 至 860 條，自 2014 年 12 月 31 日結止之短稅年開始。

FPI 為 Farmland Partners Operating Partnership, LP ("Operating Partnership") 唯一一般合夥人之唯一成員，該 Operating Partnership 於 2013 年 9 月 27 日在特拉華州成立。FPI 之所有資產均由 Operating Partnership 及其 wholly owned 子公司進行持有與營運。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，FPI 持有 Operating Partnership 98.1% 之權益。請參閱 "Note 9—Stockholders' Equity and Non-controlling Interests" 以取得關於 Operating Partnership 之 Class A Common units of limited partnership interest ("Common units"), Series A preferred units of limited partnership interest ("Series A preferred units") 及 Series B participating preferred units of limited partnership interest ("Series B participating preferred units") 之更多資訊。與持有 FPI 之 common stock (par value $0.01 per share ("common stock")) 不同，持有 Operating Partnership 之 Common units 及 Series A preferred units 之持有人通常無投票權或主導 FPI 事務之權力。作為 Operating Partnership 唯一一般合夥人之唯一成員並擁有控制權，FPI 為主要受益人，因此根據變動利益實體之合併會計標準，將 Operating Partnership 合併入帳。
提及 "Company," "we," "us," 或 "our" 意指 FPI 及其合併子公司，包括 Operating Partnership。

我們的主要戰略目標是利用我們作為北美各農業市場之高品質農地之領先機構買家、所有者及經理之地位，透過現金股息與資產增值之組合，為投資人提供強勁之風險調整回報。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有位於阿肯色州、加州、科羅拉多州、伊利諾州、印第安納州、路易斯安那州、密蘇裏州、內布拉斯加州、南卡羅來納州、德州及西維吉尼亞州之農場，總計約 71,600 英畝。此外，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有位於俄亥俄州之四家農業設備經銷商之土地與建築物，並出租予 Ag Pro Ohio, LLC ("Ag Pro")，品牌為 John Deere。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，Operating Partnership 持有 Promised Land Opportunity Zone Farms I, LLC ("OZ Fund") 9.97% 之權益，為一未合併之權益法投資，持有 11 項資產（請參閱 "Note 1—Organization and Significant Accounting Policies—Equity Method Investments"）。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們約 60% 之擁有資產（按價值計算）用於種植主要作物，如玉米、大豆、小麥、稻米及棉花，約 40% 用於生產特種作物，如杏仁、開心果、柑橘、牛油果、草莓及可食用豆類。我們相信我們之資產組合為投資人提供面對全球糧食需求增加及高品質農地日益稀缺之經濟效益，並將持續反映美國農業產出在主要作物與動物蛋白（其生產主要依賴主要作物作為飼料）之間，與特種作物之間的約略分配。
此外，我們提供貸款方案（"FPI Loan Program"），根據此方案，我們向與我們有關係之土地所有者及第三方農民（租戶及非租戶）提供貸款，以提供營運資金、土地購置、營運資金需求、農業營運活動、農業基礎設施項目及非農業營運需求之融資。
FPI Agribusiness Inc. 為一家 wholly owned 子公司（"TRS" 或 "FPI Agribusiness"），為一家可課稅之 REIT 子公司，成立目的為為本公司租戶提供大宗採購服務，並在特定情況下直接經營農場。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，TRS 在加州擁有由本公司所有之 1,845 英畝永久作物農地，並進行直接農業營運。

FPI 戰略性尋求機會，以環境友善方式利用我們之農地產生額外收入。我們在某些農場有長期租賃安排，讓經營者進行太陽能與風能生產。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們有 10 個農場，總計約 1,973 英畝，有租賃用於太陽能與風能生產或正在建設中；另外 12 個農場，總計約 4,211 英畝，有潛在未來太陽能或風能開發與營運租賃選擇權。請參閱 "–Sustainability" 以取得更多資訊。

我們的主要收入來源為租戶在我們農地上進行農業營運所支付之租金，租賃期限主要為一至三年。截至本 10-K 年度報告之日，大多數現存租賃為固定租金支付。部分租賃根據我們農場經營租戶所產生之收入計算變動租金。我們認為此固定與變動租金之組合將有助於我們抵禦農業營運之變動性，並降低我們對農場經營租戶之信貸風險，同時使我們在某些變動租賃為慣例之地區成為有吸引力之地主。然而，我們可能面臨租戶信貸風險與農業營運風險，特別是對於不需預付 100% 固定租金、變動租金安排及租賃期限超過一年之租賃。
● 稅後淨利較2024年12月31日財年結算之61.5百萬美元減少47.6%，為2025年12月31日財年結算之32.2百萬美元;
● 調整後資金來源（"AFFO"）較2024年12月31日財年結算之14.1百萬美元增加27%，為2025年12月31日財年結算之17.9百萬美元；每加權平均普通股股份之AFFO增加34.5%，為2024年12月31日財年結算之每股份0.29美元，至2025年12月31日財年結算之每股份0.39美元;
● 我們已完成在Corn Belt、Delta及South、High Plains及West Coast地區出售60處不動產，總計價為90.2百萬美元，包括2.1百萬美元之賣方融資，並認列總計價淨售價收益34.9百萬美元。在這60處不動產出售中，23處不動產用以交換贖回及註銷31,000張Series A優先單位;
● 我們已完成在Corn Belt地區收購六處不動產，總計價為7.3百萬美元;
● 總負債較2024年12月31日之204.6百萬美元減少43.0百萬美元，為2025年12月31日之161.6百萬美元;
● 我們以加權平均價格每股份11.07美元購回3,411,581張普通股股份;

FPI於2013年9月27日在馬裏蘭州成立，為運營合夥企業（Delaware limited partnership）之唯一一般合夥人之唯一成員，運營合夥企業於2013年9月27日成立。FPI所有資產均由運營合夥企業持有，且其營運主要透過運營合夥企業及其全資子公司進行。截至2025年12月31日，FPI持有98.1%的普通單位，且未持有任何A級優先單位。有關非控制性權益的更多資訊，請參閱本年度報告表10-K所附財務報表附註中的「附註9—股東權益與非控制性權益」。
FPI已選擇根據1986年美國內政部稅法第856至860條款，以REIT（不動產投資信託）方式課稅，自其短稅年度2014年12月31日開始適用。

2025 年度，本公司完成 60 間不動產的處分，位於 Corn Belt、Delta 和 South、High Plains 及 West Coast 等地區。本公司共收到 90.2 百萬美元之總計對價，包含 2.1 百萬美元之賣方融資，並認列總計出售淨收益 34.9 百萬美元。此 60 間不動產處分包含 23 間不動產，係以交換方式用以贖回及註銷 31,000 張 Series A 優先股單位（詳見下方「以不動產交換 Series A 優先股單位」段落以取得更多資訊）。
2025 年度，本公司完成 6 間不動產的收購，位於 Corn Belt 等地區。此等收購之總計對價為 7.3 百萬美元。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司於股票買回計畫下，買回 3,411,581 張本公司普通股，買回價格加權平均為每股 11.07 美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司於股票買回計畫下尚有約 17.9 百萬美元之買回餘額。去槓槓化及維持流動性地位
股票買回計畫下尚有 17.9 百萬美元的買回能力。去槓桿化與維持流動性地位
在 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度內，我們將總體負債減少 43.0 百萬美元，主要來自上述資產處置所得資金，導致流動性增加。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有 172.9 百萬美元的流動性，包含 9.3 百萬美元現金，以及在與聯邦農業抵押貸款公司（Federal Agricultural Mortgage Corporation）及其全資子公司 Farmer Mac Mortgage Securities Corporation（合稱為 "Farmer Mac"）、Metropolitan Life Insurance Company（"MetLife"）及 Rutledge Investment Company（"Rutledge"）的信貸融資下未提取的 163.6 百萬美元可用額，相較於 2024 年 12 月 31 日的現金 78.4 百萬美元及信貸融資下未提取的 167.4 百萬美元可用額。有關我們去槓桿化努力與流動性之更多資訊，請參閱 "第 7 項 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析—流動性與資本資源"。

headings: 與本公司業務及資產相關之風險
房貸債務義務使我們面臨被法拍的風險，這可能會導致我們在有房貸債務之資產或資產羣上之投資遭受損失。
我們的融資協議可能限制我們從事某些業務活動之能力，包括增加額外債務、進行資本支出及進行某些投資之能力。
基準利率上升將提高我們之借款成本，這將對我們之財務狀況、營運成果、成長前景及向股東發放現金紅利之能力產生負面影響。
利率上升將提高我們租戶之借款成本，並使其更難以取得信貸，可能會導致土地價格下跌。
全球經濟情勢，包括高通膨及供應鏈中斷，可能會對我們及我們租戶之營運產生重大且不利的影響。
約 60% 之本公司資產組合為用於種植玉米、大豆、小麥、稻米及棉花等主要農產品之農地，這使我們面臨與主要作物相關之風險。
用於種植永久性/特種作物之農地投資，其風險特質高於用於種植年度作物之農地。
未能在新市場取得成功，可能產生不利後果。
本公司並未持續監測及評估租戶信用品質，且本公司財務表現可能受到租戶財務狀況及流動性地位相關風險的影響。
本公司可能無法從財務困難或破產的租戶處收取應收租金，這可能會對本公司財務狀況、營運成果及現金流產生重大且不利的影響。
不動產投資的流動性不足，可能顯著影響本公司對不動產績效變動的應變能力，並損害本公司財務狀況。
部分州法規禁止或限制營業機構對農業用地的所有權，這可能會阻礙本公司資產組合的成長及地理多元化能力。
本公司可能因取得之不動產或未來可能取得之不動產而面臨未知或附條件責任，這可能會對本公司產生重大不利影響。
關鍵管理人員的流失，特別是 Paul A. Pittman 及 Luca Fabbri，可能對本公司執行業務策略及達成投資目標的能力產生重大不利影響。
合資企業投資可能因本公司缺乏單獨決策權、依賴合資夥伴財務狀況及與合資夥伴之間的爭議而受到不利影響。
我們可能無法實現部分或全部預期的 OZ Fund 股權投資效益。
未投保或投保不足的損失責任，可能對我們的財務狀況及現金流造成重大且不利的影響。
我們過去曾遭提起訴訟或受到威脅提起訴訟，未來亦可能遭提起訴訟，這可能導致我們需支付賠償及費用，或限制我們業務的運作。
若我們在對 Sabrepoint 提起的訴訟中未能成功，可能會產生重大且無法回收的成本。
環境相關責任的潛在賠償，可能對我們的營運成果及財務狀況造成重大且不利的影響。
paragraphs: 下列為我們認為對股東具重大影響的風險因素。您在評估本公司及其業務時，應謹慎考慮以下風險因素。下列任何因素、事件或情況的發生，可能會對我們的財務狀況、營運成果、現金流、普通股與優先股的市場價格，以及我們履行債務償還義務及向股東發放紅利的能力產生重大不利影響，進而導致股東喪失全部或部分投資。部分本報告中的陳述，包括下列風險因素中的陳述，屬於展望性陳述。請參閱本10-K年度報告開頭的「特別注意展望性陳述」部分。
我們的業務部分取決於租戶農場營運的獲利能力，若租戶農場營運持續出現獲利下滑，可能會對我們所能收取的租金金額產生重大不利影響，進而影響我們的現金流及向股東發放紅利的能力。
我們依賴租戶以產生足夠收入的方式經營我們所有的農場，使其能夠履行對我們的義務，包括支付租金與不動產稅、維持特定保險覆蓋範圍，以及維護農場的整體狀況。租戶履行租賃契約義務的能力，部分取決於其農場營運的總體獲利能力，而該獲利能力可能受到多種因素的不利影響，包括

其他因素，包括惡劣天氣條件、農產品價格、農作物病害、害蟲以及不利或不確定的政治、經濟、商業、貿易或法規環境。我們可能受到租戶農業經營業務利潤下降的影響，進而影響其支付租金的能力。此外，許多農場依賴有限數量的關鍵人員，這些人員的傷病或死亡可能影響農場的順利運作。我們無法保證，若租戶未履行租賃契約義務，我們將能及時以經濟上有利的條件重新出租或出租該農場，或甚至無法出租。此外，我們可能在執行地主權利時遭遇延誤，並可能產生重大成本以保護我們的投資。
因此，若我們租戶的農業經營業務利潤下降，或整體農業產業出現衰退，可能會對我們的財務狀況、營運成果、現金流及向股東發放紅利的能力產生重大不利影響。
我們目前有大量債務負擔，這可能使我們面臨違約債務義務的風險，限制我們的營運及擴張業務和收入的能力，並限制我們向股東發放紅利的能力。
